title: 3D Rendering Dublin: Property and Product CGI | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for Dublin developers, architects and brands: photoreal CGI for planning, off-plan sales, medtech devices, products and packaging.
h1: 3D rendering Dublin developers and brands use before anything is built
intro: 22 Signals provides 3D rendering for Dublin and Irish property developers, architects, manufacturers and brands. We produce photoreal CGI of apartment schemes, homes, interiors, medical devices, products and packaging, from still images to animated walkthroughs, so you can sell, explain or get approval for something that does not exist yet.

sections.h: Why so much Irish work starts as a render
p: Dublin needs a great many new homes, and a large share of them are apartments and build-to-rent schemes sold or let before completion. Buyers, tenants, funders, planners and local residents all want to see what a scheme will look like long before the scaffolding comes down. The same is true for products: a medtech company preparing a launch, a food or drinks brand changing its packaging, or a manufacturer showing a machine to distributors abroad.

Good CGI answers the question everyone is asking: what will this actually look like? Weak CGI raises new questions, such as why the light looks wrong, why the street seems empty, or why the product looks like plastic. We aim for images people trust.

list: Exterior views of apartment, housing and mixed-use schemes, set in their real street context.
Interiors for show apartments, amenity spaces, offices and hotels.
Aerial and massing views for funders, planning submissions and community consultation.
Animated walkthroughs and flythroughs for sales suites and websites.
Product renders for e-commerce, catalogues and trade shows.
Medical device and equipment renders, including exploded and cutaway views.
Packaging visuals for new ranges, retailer presentations and export markets.

p: Planning applications in Dublin go to one of four local authorities: Dublin City Council, Fingal, South Dublin and Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown. Larger schemes often attract close public interest, and verified views and photomontages can carry weight in how a proposal is understood. Images used in this context have to be accurate, not flattering.

For planning work we build from your architect's drawings and survey data, match camera positions to agreed viewpoints, and keep a clear record of how each image was made. Where a formal verified view methodology is required, we work with your architect or planning consultant to meet it. Sales imagery, by contrast, can show finishes, furnishings and atmosphere, and we keep the two clearly separate so marketing images are never presented as planning evidence.

Irish property buyers search on Daft.ie and MyHome.ie, and listing photos decide whether people click. For a scheme that is still a hole in the ground, renders do that job. We produce a set designed for the portals and your website: hero exteriors, key interiors, the views from upper floors, amenity spaces and the local streets. We also prepare floor-plan visuals and short animations for social ads.

Accuracy matters for trust and for consumer protection. We work from the actual specification, show finishes the buyer will really receive, and mark images as computer generated where you choose to, so the sales team never has to explain away a difference.

Ireland has a large medtech and pharma sector, and many companies need to show devices that are small, complex or not yet manufactured. 3D lets us show internal mechanisms, cross-sections and step-by-step use in a way photography cannot. Because these images often appear in training, investor and regulatory materials, every claim and label is checked against your approved information, and your reviewers sign off each view.

For consumer goods, food and drink brands we produce product and packaging renders that work on retailer sites, in trade presentations and on social media, and can be updated quickly when a label or flavour changes.

Because our team also produces video, motion graphics and 3D animation, the models we build for stills can become walkthroughs, product animations and ad content without starting again. That is often where the value lies: one well-built model serves the planning pack, the sales brochure, the website, the launch film and a year of social posts.

list: Irish light: soft, often overcast skies and low winter sun, not the hard blue skies of a stock library.
Real context: the actual neighbouring buildings, street trees, bus stops and cycle lanes, taken from site photography.
Honest materials: brick, render, timber and glazing that match the specification sheet, with believable wear and reflections.
People and life: a few residents, bikes and cars in proportion, rather than empty streets or crowded fantasy scenes.
Correct scale: furniture, ceiling heights and room sizes that match the floor plans, so buyers are not misled.
p: We review every draft against these points before you see it, which keeps revision rounds short and the final set consistent.

list: Talk: a 15-minute call about what you need to show, to whom and by when.
Plan: a written brief within 5 to 7 days listing views, references, materials, formats and delivery dates.
Build: modelling, lighting and materials, with draft views for comment before final renders, and dates in writing.
Grow: extra views, seasonal or interior variations, animations and updates as the design changes.

sections.h: Remote production, site visits when useful
p: Rendering is produced remotely, with review calls booked around your team's calendar and every comment tracked against the draft it refers to. For context photography, site visits or a sales suite launch, we can travel to Dublin and plan that into the scope.

list: Number of views and their complexity.
Whether drawings and models already exist or must be built from scratch.
Level of context: a plain background versus a full street scene.
Animation length and resolution.
Number of revision rounds, and changes to the design during production.

faqs.q: What does 3D rendering Dublin developers commission usually include?
faqs.a: A set of exterior and interior stills, often with aerial views and a short animation, produced from the architect's drawings and the sales specification. Many also order floor-plan visuals and social media cuts for the launch.

faqs.q: Can your renders be used in planning applications?
faqs.a: Yes, when produced for that purpose. We build from drawings and survey data, match agreed viewpoints and record how each image was made. Where a formal verified view method is required, we work with your architect or planning consultant to meet it.

faqs.q: What files do you need to start?
faqs.a: Architectural drawings or CAD and BIM files, a materials and finishes schedule, site photos if available, and examples of the style you like. For products, CAD files or detailed photos and dimensions.

faqs.q: How long does a rendering project take?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of views and whether models exist already. The written brief after the 5 to 7 day planning stage sets out each delivery date, and we share drafts before final renders.

faqs.q: Can you render medical devices accurately?
faqs.a: Yes. We work from CAD data, show internal parts, cutaways and steps of use, and check every label and claim against your approved information with your reviewers before delivery.

faqs.q: Can the 3D models be reused later?
faqs.a: Yes. The models can be used for new views, animations, interactive content and ads. You receive the final files, and we can keep the models updated as the design changes.
